reason: The text does not discuss or support the statement that priests are the most important group in society. This passage from Exodus 8-11 focuses on the plagues inflicted upon Egypt (frogs, boils, hail, locusts, darkness) and God's power over Pharaoh and his kingdom. While Egyptian magicians/sorcerers (חרטומים - hartumim) are mentioned briefly in the boils plague narrative, they are portrayed as powerless and unable to stand before Moses due to the plague. These figures are not identified as priests, and the text makes no claims about the social or religious importance of any priestly class. The narrative centers on the conflict between Pharaoh and Moses, and God's demonstrations of power.
